newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi to soon get $170 mln from tobacco cos..
newsitem.headline: Mississippi to soon get $170 mln from tobacco cos..

text.p: The tobacco industry's settlement of Mississippi's Medicaid suit against cigarette companies provides for a payment to the state of $170 million by July 15, the companies said Thursday.
The agreement in principle would be superseded by the broader, comprehensive tobacco accord pending before Congress.
The tobacco companies said that beginning in December 1998, they will pay Mississippi a 1.7 percent share of the annual payments to be made to the states.
Without giving effect to adjustments for inflation and changes in sales volume, this could result in payments to Mississippi of $68 million in 1998 and $76.5 million in 1999.
The payments will scale up to $136 million by the sixth year and continue at that level, the companies said.

The companies issuing the statement were Philip Morris Cos Inc ; R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp ; Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc, and Lorillard Tobacco Co, a unit of Loews Corp.
